apps.name: Skate 3
apps.subtitle: Locked 60fps. Bring your own copy of the game.
apps.localizedDescription:
A static recompilation of Skate 3 for iOS, rendering through Vulkan on MoltenVK. Runs at a locked 60fps on an iPhone 13 mini (A15): median frame 16.7ms, 95th percentile 16.8-17.8ms.

YOU MUST SUPPLY THE GAME. This app contains no game content and will not start without it.

AFTER INSTALLING:
1. Connect your iPhone to a computer and open Finder > your iPhone > Files > Skate 3 (on Windows, iTunes > File Sharing).
2. Drop in a 'game' folder containing your own disc files. That is about 6GB, so allow a few minutes.
3. Add Title Update 3, the free update EA published on Xbox Live - it is not on the disc and the game will not run without it. The app can download it for you: choose "Install the title update" and then Download. If you would rather supply it yourself, copy the package into the same Skate 3 folder and it is found automatically.

The setup screens walk you through steps 2 and 3.

On-screen touch controls appear when no controller is attached; MFi and Bluetooth controllers are picked up automatically. Press Start + Select together for a performance menu that shows your frame rate and what is limiting it.

Requires iOS 16.0 or later.

versions.localizedDescription:
iOS skipped a release: this carries everything Android got in v0.2.0, and then some.

Controller remapping. Sixteen inputs - face buttons, bumpers, triggers, stick clicks, D-pad, Back and Start - can each be moved to any other, on the Controls page under Button Mapping. The sticks themselves are not remapped; Swap Sticks and Invert Camera Y already cover that.

Three bugs that were costing frames. Touching the Framerate Cap row silently erased the shipped 60 fps cap on every later launch, because one setting's name was a prefix of another's. A per-packet GPU profiler was running in every build - about 1.7 million clock reads a second - whether or not anyone was profiling. And the ceiling that lets a frame advance more than one simulation period had been compiled for Switch only, so the two platforms whose frames overrun it most never had it.

Eleven new settings rows aimed at buying frames back on a phone: 3D Scene Resolution, draw distance down to an eighth, NPC and World update rates, cuts for pedestrians and traffic, movable props and other skaters, vegetation, hair, water, draw batching, 40/45/50 fps caps, and an FPS Percentiles readout that shows the 1% low and p95/p99 next to the average - the average is exactly the statistic that hides a stutter.

First launch could previously come up blank, roughly one clean install in ten: parts of a screen drawn once while their shaders were still compiling were skipped and never came back. Shader compilation now stays synchronous through the cold-boot frontend.

New installs ship at Half draw distance. If you are updating, your existing video settings are kept exactly as they are.

The crowd and prop cuts are ported from darchap's Skate3-Port, which did them first.

The title update can now be installed from inside the app. Before this, iOS could do neither half of it: the "select a file" route went through the system document picker, which does not work under TrollStore or on a jailbreak, and the download button was never shown at all - so players who had just installed from a disc image could install the game and then not the update it requires. Now you can download it in the app (1.7 MB, no computer involved), or copy the package into your Skate 3 folder and have it found automatically, the way disc images have been found since 2.6.0.

The app opens on a home screen instead of straight into the game: Play, install from a disc image, install the title update, choose a map pack, and save a diagnostic report you can share from the Files app.

Settings now stick. Twenty-four rows were being forced back to their defaults at every launch - resolution, V-Sync, MSAA, shadows, ambient occlusion, bloom, sun shafts, draw distance, the frame cap, and the audio and interface rows. The menu wrote your choice and startup overwrote it on the way back in. Opening and closing the menu also used to freeze the per-device memory budgets at whatever that launch picked; it no longer writes rows you did not touch.

Map pack names appear in other languages. A pack built for one market leaves the other languages empty and the game showed those empty slots - an unnamed entry in the map list and raw identifiers where level names belong, reported as the DLC maps not loading in French or Spanish. Names now fall back to English. Fixed in the game rather than in the packs, so it applies to packs you already have.

Fixes the slowdown on mission completion and replay screens. Finished graphics work was being cleaned up at a fixed 256 items per frame even on the path meant to have no limit, so once a screen produced them faster than that the backlog only grew, every frame paid for it, and the frame rate decayed toward single digits until iOS killed the app. Measured on an iPhone 13 mini: a backlog of 18,000 falling by exactly 255 a frame for seventy frames, one of those cleanups finishing its share in half a millisecond and stopping anyway.

Also fixes a quit-to-home after switching away and back. GPU work that iOS refuses while an app is in the background keeps failing for a few milliseconds after it returns, and those failures were charged to a budget meant for one occasional error every few seconds - eight of them arrived inside 20 milliseconds and the app reported a lost graphics device.

Installing the game no longer depends on the system file picker, which does not work under TrollStore or on a jailbreak. Drop your disc image into the Skate 3 folder in Files and it is found automatically. An extracted disc copied across as a folder is now accepted too, instead of being reported as missing.

Adds a Texture Memory setting under Settings > Video, 256 MB through 768 MB, applied immediately. The default is unchanged from 2.5.0; raising it helps most if challenge completions slow the game down, at the cost of resident memory.

Requires a 6-core device - every iPhone that runs iOS 16 qualifies, but older iPads (A9/A9X/A10/A10X) do not and will not run it. The game no longer instruments itself while you play: the frame-timing tools that ran on every frame are off, behind a Diagnostics switch in Settings > System. The settings menu asks before it closes the game, and its buttons are sized for a thumb. Adds a Potato preset and a Half draw-distance setting. Also carries every unpublished fix since 2.4.0 - ProMotion iPhones stuck at 30 fps, every iPhone running at half rate, the permanent black screen with audio still playing, and the background-GPU session kill.

A performance menu on Start + Select that shows your frame rate and what is limiting it, more controller options (vibration strength, deadzones, invert Y, rebindable shortcuts), and setup that explains how to get the game and the title update onto your phone. Supersedes all earlier releases.
Sustained 60fps, on-screen touch controls, and no game content in the bundle.
